# Engine port provenance

Every file under `engine/` traces to a `packages/core/src/` file in
[`dgreenberggit/tbc-gear-prio`](https://github.com/dgreenberggit/tbc-gear-prio)
(the private repo this fork's parent detour lives in), at commit:

```
12ce58414ad0f8f1e34c581d7583e6998e05e8bb
```

`git rev-parse HEAD` in that repo, run on the `feat/shopping-list-wowsims-tab`
branch, 2026-08-14.

This file is the compensating control named in `docs/plans/wowsims-tab/plan.md`
§8 ("E-W3 runs here, not in the fork"): the hash column is what
`scripts/check_engine_port_drift.py` (in the `tbc-gear-prio` repo) re-derives
and compares on every `pnpm verify`. **A hash match proves the file's bytes
have not changed since this table was written — nothing about behaviour.**
Only the parity test (E-W3, `packages/core/test/wowsims-fork-parity.test.ts`)
proves behaviour is unchanged.

## Two rows trace to a later core commit than the header

`dead-slots.ts` and `plausibility.ts` carry a source-commit note in their
label column: they trace to core `2e6b257` ("Mark worn-unrankable slots
instead of showing false losses"), which is **not** an ancestor of the header
commit above:

```
git merge-base --is-ancestor 2e6b257 12ce58414ad0f8f1e34c581d7583e6998e05e8bb   && echo ancestor || echo "not an ancestor"
```

The `worn-unrankable` feature landed in core after this table was written, so
the two files sat stale while their "none (import paths only)" labels stayed
literally accurate for the commit they were compared against — which is why
neither gate could see it (ticket 214). The port was applied 2026-08-17 and
both files now show zero comment-stripped code divergence from their core
sources.

The header commit is stale for **every** row, not just these two. Re-baselining
the whole table is deliberately not done here: it would assert a fresh
comparison for 31 rows nobody re-verified in this round. Recorded as an open
observation on ticket 214 instead.

## Racing removed 2026-08-22

`rank.ts`, `view.ts` and `content-hash.ts` (doc comment only) no longer carry
candidate-pool.md M2's racing pass, and `promotion.ts` is deleted — its row is
gone from the table below, because the drift script reports a listed file that
is absent as `missing:` and fails.

Ported from core commit `28b00f9` ("Remove racing; full-sweep every eligible
candidate"), the change ADR-0026 records; the ADR itself was written in
`66dab19`. That commit is **later than this file's header commit** and not an
ancestor of it:

```
git merge-base --is-ancestor 28b00f9 12ce58414ad0f8f1e34c581d7583e6998e05e8bb
# exit 1 — not an ancestor
```

`rank.ts` was **not** re-ported from core. The removal was done in place, so
the fork keeps its three deliberate adaptations (`canonicalJson` hashing, no
`spec.ts`, `simDatabaseFor` threading). Two divergences from core survive on
purpose and must not be "fixed" by copying core's file: the cache payload
freezes three racing fields where core freezes four (no `promoteTopJ`, which
the fork never hashed — adding it would change every key already written), and
`candidateCap` is hashed as `?? ordered.length` where core omits it when
undefined. Compare the two files by hand, not with `diff -w`.

E-W3 (`packages/core/test/wowsims-fork-parity.test.ts`) passed against the
de-raced engine before these hashes were written, which is the order this
file's own rule requires.

## Line endings

`scripts/check_engine_port_drift.py` hashes each ported file's bytes on disk
and does not normalize line endings, so a file's hash depends on the line
endings it has on disk.

Earlier rounds recorded a trap in an older fork clone that had
`core.autocrlf=true`: checkout wrote CRLF to disk while git stored LF, and the
check reported files as drifted for line endings alone. That no longer
describes the clone. Measured on 2026-10-08 in the port worktree's fork clone:

- `git -C vendor/tbc-new-fork config core.autocrlf` prints `false`.
- `git -C vendor/tbc-new-fork ls-files --eol ui/features/upgrades/model/engine`
  showed every ported `.ts` file as `i/lf w/lf` except `plausibility.ts`, which
  git stored with CRLF (`i/crlf w/crlf`). Since the oxfmt commit of
  § Comment sweep for the upstream PR, `plausibility.ts` is LF too: on
  2026-11-18 the same command printed `i/lf w/lf` for all 38 files.
- `sha256sum` of `set-value.ts` and `disclosure.ts` on disk equals the hash
  recorded for each in the table below.

A clone with `core.autocrlf=true` would again write CRLF to disk and fail the
check without any content change. If that happens, compare the hash of
`tr -d '\r' < <file> | sha256sum` with the recorded one before treating it as drift.

## Seed spacing ported (ticket 530)

`se.ts` is a byte copy of core's `packages/core/src/se.ts`, so check it with
`cmp` against core, not against the header commit above. `rank.ts` takes
core's `defaultSeedsFor` and the two-argument guard in place. E-W3 passed
before the `se.ts` and `rank.ts` hashes moved.

## Re-homed to `ui/features/upgrades/model/engine/` (ticket 558, 2026-10-05)

Upstream deleted `ui/core` in its React rewrite, so the engine moved from
`ui/core/components/individual_sim_ui/upgrades/engine/` (fork branch
`feat/upgrades-tab` at `cb561067`) to this folder on `feat/upgrades-tab-react`,
branched from upstream `42c75dc9` (upstream `5262ff38` merged in on 2026-10-09;
its two commits touch no engine file). Only import lines changed: relative imports
lost their `.js` extension (upstream's `import/extensions` lint rule), and
imports of upstream modules became alias paths (`@generated/proto/common`,
`@sim/proto/database`, `@sim/proto/gems`, `@sim/proto/items`). The 28 rows whose
file has such an import were re-hashed (`bulk/partition.ts` changed too but
has no row). Check the claim per file with
`git diff cb561067:ui/core/components/individual_sim_ui/upgrades/engine/rank.ts HEAD:ui/features/upgrades/model/engine/rank.ts`,
which shows import hunks only. Comments that name old upstream paths (`ui/core/...`) were left as they
were, because a comment edit here is an engine edit. E-W3 runs from the main
repo once its harness reads this folder (ticket 558, chunk K2), so these
hashes moved before E-W3 ran against them; that is the one exception to this
file's order.

## Comment sweep for the upstream PR (ticket 344, 2026-11-17)

Every ported file's comments were cut to wowsims' register, and citations of
this repo (ADRs, PLAN.md, tickets, `packages/core` paths) were removed, so
the fork's comments no longer match core's. Code is unchanged: for each file,
the TypeScript AST with comments removed equals the one at fork `1410a775e`
(`.scratch/pr-prep/code-same.cjs` in the main checkout, gitignored; the
review file `docs/reviews/chore-344-pr-prep.md` records its output). So `se.ts` is no
longer a byte copy of core's file (§ Seed spacing ported); compare it to core
with comments stripped, and read "byte-for-byte" in the table below as code
only. E-W3 passed on the swept files before all 36 hashes moved.

The fork commit after it ran upstream's formatter (`oxfmt`, which upstream CI
runs as `npm run fmt`) over the engine, so the files now use tabs and single
quotes and `plausibility.ts` is LF (§ Line endings). Its AST equals the
comment sweep's with quotes, commas, parentheses and comments ignored
(`.scratch/pr-prep/ast-same.cjs`). E-W3 passed again before the hashes moved a
second time. `scripts/check_engine_port_drift.py` reads the fork's unions in
either quote style since then.

The pre-merge review's fixes (2026-11-18, fork `c922f7efc`, `9908e365b`,
`6b0acba94` and `e8de08ded`) thinned the engine's comments further, corrected
stale ones and put coined terms in plain words. Their AST still equals fork
`1410a775e`'s, by the review's script. E-W3 passed before 28 hashes moved,
in two rounds.

The naming pass after it (2026-11-18, fork `1b18e5fae`, `c04da370b` and
`b23f50100`) changed code names, not behaviour, and 14 hashes moved after
E-W3 passed. `DEFAULT_SEED_COUNT` and `isReplicable` now live in `se.ts`,
where the tab's progress tracker reads them; `view.ts` exports `zoneKeyOf`;
pseudo-stats, gem quality, item type and socket colour use the generated
enums. Renames that the rows below still give by their old names:
`measureBrokenSetValue` is `measureSetBonuses`, `pricesHitBySpells` is
`usesSpellHitBudget`, `trackExpertise` is `hasExpertiseCap`, `versionGears`
and `VersionGears` are `requestsPerLayout` and `RequestsPerLayout`,
`markedSetIds` is `setIdsWithoutBonuses`, and `InflationKey`'s `membersPkg`,
`members2pc`, `pkgEnd`, `twoPcEnd` and `B` are `piecesBreakingAlone`,
`twoPcPiecesBreakingAlone`, `allPiecesBreak`, `allTwoPcPiecesBreak` and
`brokenBonusDps`. `packages/core/src` keeps `trackExpertise`; the drift check
compares bytes and three unions, not names.

The review's last comment fixes (2026-11-18, fork `99c27adc8`) moved the
`rank.ts` and `view.ts` hashes after E-W3 passed; the AST equals
`b23f50100`'s, by the review's script.

Two more renames (2026-11-18, fork `1283e6eb7`) moved the `rank.ts` and
`set-screen.ts` hashes after E-W3 passed. The rows below still say `statsAt`,
which is now `sumOfSinglesDpsAt`, since it returns a DPS estimate. The tab's
`DEFAULT_ITERATIONS` (`run_state.ts`, not ported) is now
`TAB_DEFAULT_ITERATIONS`. The engine's 5000 keeps the core name, so the
`rank.ts` row stays true. The AST equals `99c27adc8`'s once the old names map
to the new ones.

The naming review after it (2026-11-18/19, fork `1283e6eb7`..`2ab306bcc`)
renamed code identifiers in the fork only, not in core, with no behaviour
change; E-W3 passed before all 22 hashes moved. `packages/core/src` keeps every
old name, so the rows and the notes above still give these by their old names
(each one is now, in the fork):

- own and its deltas: `IndividualDelta` → `OwnDelta`,
  `individualDeltasByItemId` → `ownDeltasByItemId`, `singleSwapBreaks` →
  `ownSwapBreaks`; the rule-Z estimate `sumOfSinglesEstimate` →
  `estimateCombinedDelta`, and `statsAt`/`sumOfSinglesDpsAt` →
  `estimatedDeltaAt`.
- partner combinations: `partnerSets` → `partnerCombinations`,
  `choosePartnerSet` → `choosePartners`.
- added pieces, bonus and gear (the "package" word): `selectPackage` →
  `selectAddedPieces`, `ScreenPackage` → `ScreenGear`, `packageAt` → `gearAt`,
  `packagesInReach` → `addedByCount`, `topMeasuredPackage` → `topMeasuredBonus`,
  `memberPackages` → `bonusesWithItem`, `substitutedPackageBreaks` →
  `topBonusBreaksWithRow`.
- counts (the "ladder" and "rung" words): `measureWornSetLadder` →
  `measureWornSetCounts`, `rungSimmer` → `countSimmer`, `BonusCountPredicate` →
  `CountsAsBreak`.
- credit, inflation and thresholds: `walkCredit` → `creditBreakdown`,
  `lostThresholds` → `brokenThresholds`, `computeSynergy` → `computeBonusDps`,
  `InflationKey` → `InflationTerm` (its fields are unchanged),
  `setIdsWithoutBonuses` → `setIdsNotValued`, `nextMeasurableThreshold` →
  `nextImplementedThreshold`, `repairHitCap` → `repairHitBudget`,
  `RequestsPerLayout` → `RequestsPerCopyLayout`.
- meta recolour, British spelling to American: `repairAndMinimize` →
  `repairMetaGems`, and `colour`/`recolour` are `color`/`recolor` throughout.
- the set-step, best-stop and gate words moved in the code and in the
  recordings' stored keys together, by the owner's 2026-11-18 ruling:
  `measureSetSteps` → `measureBonusGear`, `walkSteps` → `bonusGearCredit`,
  `stepRanking` → `bonusGearMeasured`, `stepGearDps` → `bonusGearDps`,
  `setStepSims` → `bonusGearSims`, `stepFutureUnmeasured` →
  `bonusGearUnmeasured`, `SetPotentialStep` → `SetPotentialIncrement`,
  `stepEligible` → `canBeCredited`; `crossingGates` → `crossingChecks`,
  `belowGate` → `belowNoise`.
- run notes (the "substitution" word): `Substitution` → `RunNote`,
  `uniqueSubstitutions` → `uniqueNotes`, and the `*SkipSubstitution` helpers →
  `*SkipNote` (`setBonusesSkipSubstitution` → `setBonusCountsSkipNote`,
  `breakSplitSkipSubstitution` → `breakSplitSkipNote`,
  `setScreenSkipSubstitution` → `setScreenSkipNote`, `wornSetSkipSubstitution` →
  `wornSetSkipNote`).
- the pre-merge review of the naming review (2026-11-19, fork
  `9f8dd091a`..`e08efd6ec`): `thresholdLostByDroppingOnePiece` →
  `thresholdBrokenByDroppingOnePiece` in `dead-slots.ts`; the rest were locals
  and comments. E-W3 passed before the six hashes moved.
- ticket 888 and the American spelling pass (2026-11-19, fork
  `a58638ea1`..`93027b6c9`): `bonusGearMeasured` → `usesBonusGear` (in the
  stored keys too), meta repair's `hitCap` option → `hitBudget` and
  `wornHitCap` → `wornHitBudget`, the bonus term's `have` → `worn`, and
  comments spelled the American way. E-W3 passed before the five hashes moved.

The drift check compares bytes and the three unions, not names.

## Set-aside tidy (tickets 886 and 887, 2026-11-20)

Ticket 886 (fork `697f84ca3`, comment reworded in `6ca79f308`): `rank.ts`'s set screen takes the set's own
crossing-check value out of its estimate once per added piece, since each own
delta already reached that bonus alone; `set-screen.ts` comments only. Ticket
887 (fork `57035ec23`, two messages reworded in `6ca79f308`) is fork-only tidying, and core keeps its own copies:

- `fixtures/report-events-offline.ts` and `fixtures/slamaltman-offline.ts`
  are deleted (nothing imported them), so their rows are gone from the table.
- Deleted for having no caller: `disclosure.ts`'s `renderDisclosure`,
  `fightProvenanceLines`, `setPotentialDisclosureLine` and `CONFIDENT_PARSE`;
  `pool.ts`'s `UniverseEntry`, `poolEntryFromUniverse`, `poolFromUniverse`,
  `filterPoolByZone`, `zonesInPool`, `bossesInPool`, `VIEW_ALL`,
  `viewFilterValue`, `validateViewFilter` and `PoolEntry.curationHint`;
  `items.ts`'s `isEnchantable`; `view.ts`'s `ViewOptions.hideWorn`;
  `seams/gear-source.ts`'s `CachingGearSource` and `gearCacheKey`.
- Fields filled but never read: `meta-repair.ts`'s `GemRecolor.cost` and
  `dead-slots.ts`'s `DeadSlot.poolSize`.
- `pool.ts`'s `SimSlotName` is `slots.ts`'s `SimOrderName`, not a second copy
  of the union; `set-bonus.ts` imports `setCounts` and `setNameOf` from
  `set-value.ts`.
- `plausibility.ts` messages are reworded, and `dead-slots.ts`'s cause
  `set-break-toll` is `set-break-cost`, so they differ from core's text.
- `partner-choice.ts`'s `estimateCombinedDelta` takes
  `Pick<PartnerQuery, 'row' | 'brokenBy' | 'breakDps'>`; three `rank.ts` log
  lines say "added pieces" where they said "package".

E-W3 (`packages/core/test/wowsims-fork-parity.test.ts`) passed on these files
before their hashes moved.

## Pre-PR removals (ticket 885, 2026-11-20)

Fork-only changes before the upstream pull request; core keeps its own
copies. Owner, on ticket 885: "Sure, yes".

- Removed because only this repo's tests reached them (fork `ac2353f6f`):
  the partner rules other than `close-calls`, with `Deps.partnerRule` and the
  rule argument to `choosePartners` (`partner-choice.ts`, `rank.ts`); the
  partner audit (`PartnerAudit`, `PartnerAuditEntry`, `Ranking.partnerAudit`);
  the set screen's `'record'` mode (`set-screen.ts`, `rank.ts`; `'off'` and
  `'on'` stay); `estimateCombinedDelta`'s `includeCombinationOnlyBreaks`
  option, which every remaining caller set to true; and in `view.ts` the `'split'` credit view
  and the `'full-path'` rule, so `rankableSetPotential`,
  `setPotentialCredit`, `setPotentialTerms`, `setPotentialIncrements` and
  `applyView` always use the full view at the highest-credit bonus.
  `seams/sim-runner.ts` changed in a comment only. The rows in § Ported files still name
  `'split'`, full-path and the other rules as history. What the tab runs and
  its cache keys are unchanged: an unset rule or screen mode was already
  absent from the hashed object.
- `se.ts`'s two `DegenerateSeedsError` messages and one `disclosure.ts`
  assumption no longer cite this repo's plan or tickets (fork `3215ba095`),
  and a `set-screen.ts` comment no longer names ticket 886 (fork `dadfad891`).
  So `se.ts` no longer matches core byte for byte, and the `cmp` check in
  § Seed spacing ported is history.

E-W3 (`packages/core/test/wowsims-fork-parity.test.ts`) passed on these files
before their hashes moved.

## Store faults are internal (tickets 890 and 891, 2026-11-22)

Fork `8628857ec`; core keeps its own copies. A store read or write that fails
now stops the run with `RankError('internal')` wherever it happens, as the sim
cache's own calls already did:

- `rank.ts`: `rankUpgrades`' own store calls (the saved-ranking read and
  write, the job row's create and updates) go through `asInternal`, which
  `sim-calls.ts` now exports.
- `set-phase.ts`, `set-less-copies.ts`, `set-screen.ts`: the set sims'
  runners return a failed sim as `{ simError }` in place of throwing it, so
  `measureSameGearBonus`, `measureWornSetCounts` and the set screen catch
  nothing and a store fault is no longer taken as a failed sim.
  `sim-calls.ts`'s `runSimAt` is gone; the set screen calls `simOrFailure`.

E-W3 (`packages/core/test/wowsims-fork-parity.test.ts`) passed on these files
before their hashes moved.

## How to read "Adaptation"

- **none** — byte-for-byte port apart from import paths.
- **adapted** — same logic, retargeted at a different data source or API;
  the file's own doc comment explains the change in full.
- **not ported** — listed for completeness; plan §2.1 excludes it and the
  reason is in plan §2.1 or in the substituting file's own doc comment.

Ticket 863 (fork-only): every failed set-phase sim adds a line with the sim's own error: the same-gear and crossing gates and the worn-1 pair sim (`SET_BONUS_SKIP_REASONS.simFailed`), the step sims (`rowSimsFailed`), the bonus-off sims (`breakSplitSkipSubstitution`: the step stays measured, only its break is not split from its pieces), each line once through `uniqueSubstitutions`, keyed on the text the page shows because a Go panic's stack trace differs from sim to sim, the set screen (`setScreenSkipSubstitution`) and the worn-set ladder (`wornSetSkipSubstitution`, which names the set and no count, since the ladder does not know which counts hold a bonus). `measuringSimsFailed` became `measuringSimsNotBuilt`, for a gate whose requests could not be built. E-W3 re-run green. Ticket 867 (fork-only): a set whose bonus counts were not read, because the read failed or its largest package failed gem repair, adds a line with that error (`setBonusesSkipSubstitution`, reasons `bonusListFailed` and `metaOff`). E-W3 re-run green. Ticket 870 (fork-only): a worn-set ladder count whose sim failed is counted as a break only when the sim lists a bonus at that count (`wornSetBonusCounts`: the bonuses active on the worn gear that go when the set is sent set-less); when that list cannot be read, the count is counted as before and a `setBonusesSkipSubstitution` line gives the error. E-W3 re-run green. Ticket 869 (fork-only): `VersionGears` gives a `BuildFailure` with the caught error in place of an undefined entry, so the same-gear and crossing gates add a line ending in that error (`SET_BONUS_SKIP_REASONS.notBuilt`) and the set screen adds one (`setScreenSkipSubstitution` with `notBuilt`); the step gear, step break split and worn-1 pair still give no line (ticket 872). E-W3 re-run green. Ticket 871 (fork-only): when the bonus list fails too, `wornSetBonusCounts` gives no counts, so no failed ladder count is counted as a break; the ladder and read lines say what was not measured. E-W3 re-run green. Ticket 874 (fork-only): each failure line keeps the error in `Substitution.error` and the tab's one sentence in `detail` (`SkipReason`, `withError`); a candidate line's error ends with its item id and slot, for the console. E-W3 re-run green. Ticket 872 (fork-only): the package sim, step gear, step break split and worn-1 pair give a line ending in the build error (`notBuilt`, `rowsNotBuilt`, `breakSplitSkipSubstitution` with `notBuilt`); a step gear or worn-1 pair whose gem repair fails gives the `metaOff` line; the worn set's bonus-list request that cannot be built gives `bonusListNotBuilt`. E-W3 re-run green. Owner's ruling 2026-11-11 (fork-only, tickets 874 and 868): `Substitution.error` holds only a failed call's own error, word for word, because the run's one error toast shows the first one; a candidate line's item id and slot follow its sentence in `detail`, and a gem repair that finds no swap (a `kind: "repair"` candidate skip, `metaOff`) is no failed call, so its rule follows the sentence in `detail` and it has no `error`. E-W3 re-run green. Ticket 521 (fork-only): `Ranking.caps`, `RankedItem.hitDriven` and `RankedItem.hitRegression` deleted, with the `capStateFrom` call and the per-candidate stat delta that fed the two flags; the ranking's other fields and every composed request are unchanged (E-W3 re-run green). Review A1 of `fix/867-870-tab-errors` (fork-only): `versionGears` gives a `RepairFailure` in place of a `BuildFailure` when a version's rebuild fails its gem repair, and `onRepairFailed` is gone, so each caller handles it as the same failure on its own build: the package loop skips the package with the `metaOff` line, the set screen leaves the rung unmeasured with no line, the crossing gate leaves the gate unmeasured with no line, the step gear gives the `metaOff` reason, the break split is skipped with no line, and the worn-1 pair gives the `metaOff` line; none carries `Substitution.error`. E-W3 re-run green. Review N3 of `fix/867-870-tab-errors` (fork-only): `uniqueSubstitutions` keeps a later line with an `error` in place of an earlier one with the same sentence and none, so the console and the run's error toast keep the failed call's error. E-W3 re-run green. Ticket 623 (fork-only): the worn-set ladder, same-gear, crossing and step-gear gates get the `Cutoff`, so they gate at `absDps`, not √2 × it; `setBonusNoiseFloorDps` is no longer imported. E-W3 re-run green. Split into `rank-types.ts`, `rank-setup.ts`, `run-notes.ts`, `sim-calls.ts`, `hit-budget.ts`, `gear-swap.ts`, `rank-candidates.ts`, `rank-replication.ts` and the `set-*.ts` files by the 2026-11-21 readability plan (`.scratch/agent-reports/2026-11-21-design-task-upgrades-readability-plan.md`): whole declarations moved word for word, and `rank.ts` re-exports every name it exported. | `set-less-copies.ts`   | none — fork-only, no core ancestor                           | fork-only (tickets 511 and 512) — `SET_LESS_ID_OFFSET` and `SET_KEPT_ID_OFFSET`, `applyCopies` (a request with the listed slots' items swapped for set-less copies at id + 1,000,000, each with a copied database row whose `setName` is "" and `setId` 0, or for set-kept copies at id + 2,000,000, whose row changes only `id`), `applySetLessCopies` (set-less copies only), `measureSameGearBonus` (the same gear simmed twice with the first set pieces in slot order sent as copies in both requests, set-kept in one and set-less in the other, so an effect Go keys by item id cancels) and `clearsSameGearGate` (a value above both the noise floor and twice its se), and `measureWornSetLadder` (a worn set's value at every count from 2 to its worn count: rung R(c) keeps the first piece real, sends pieces 2 … c as set-kept copies and the rest as set-less copies, and count c is R(c) − R(c − 1); ticket 512). Nothing in core measures a set bonus this way, so there is no source to compare; `fork-set-net.test.ts` cases 511-C, 511-G, 511-H and 512-W, 512-P, 512-N, 512-H, 512-C cover it. Ticket 535: `measureSameGearBonus` takes an optional `requestsFor`, called once for "on" and "off", so each can wear the gems repair chose for its own hit (ADR-0035 amendment); without it both requests are `composedRequest` with copies, as before. Ticket 852: a rejection from `requestsFor` is no longer caught as a failed sim, so a failed set-version stats read fails the run. Ticket 863: `measureSameGearBonus` returns a `SimFailure` with the sim's error when a sim fails (still undefined when no request could be built), and `measureWornSetLadder` takes an optional `onSimFailed(error)` for each failed rung. `fork-set-net.test.ts` cases 476-D, 511-U, 863-X and 863-L cover it. Ticket 869: `measureSameGearBonus` returns a `BuildFailure` with the error when a request cannot be built. Ticket 872: `measureWornSetLadder` builds each rung before its sim, so a rung that cannot be built goes to `onFailed` with `notBuilt`. Ticket 623: `clearsSameGearGate` takes the `Cutoff` and passes a value above `max(absDps, 2·se)`, so no caller can hand it the √2 floor. | `set-screen.ts`        | none — fork-only, no core ancestor                           | fork-only (ticket 511 K5R and K5ON) — the set screen. Record mode: `recordSetScreen` runs, for each gain-side set with at least 2 counts between its worn count and its reach, the pair (rungs 0 and R − w on the package's gear at its reach, at N = 10, 100, 300 and 1000) and the ladder (every rung, at N = 100, 300 and 1000), where rung k sends the first k added pieces as set-kept copies and the rest as set-less copies (`set-less-copies.ts`'s `applyCopies`); every sim asks for per-iteration values, and `pairedSe` is sd(a_i − b_i)/√N; it filters nothing. On mode (K5ON, the tab's default): `runSetScreenOn` runs only the pair at `SCREEN_ON_RULE.iterations` (300) through the same rung builder (`rungSimmer`), so an on-mode pair is the record mode's request at that N; a set's M2 is its best package estimate (the caller's `statsAt`) plus the pair; σ = √2 · baseline stdev / √300; `applyScreenRule`, a port of `apply_rule` in the K5E scorer `score_screen.py` (rule 1 exact zero first, absent readings kept, rule 2, top K = 2, band c = 1), gives each set kept or dropped with a reason. `SCREEN_ON_RULE`'s constants are rule constants, not a set table. Each reading catches its own failure, and a set whose readings failed is kept. It holds no table of set ids or piece counts. Nothing in core screens sets, so there is no source to compare; `fork-set-net.test.ts` cases 511-SR, 511-SZ and 511-SF (record mode) and 511-SU, 511-SN, 511-SB, 511-SD, 511-SA, 511-SL and 511-SH (on mode) cover it. Ticket 533: `SetScreenInput.signal?`, the caller's Stop. Once it has aborted, a failed reading writes no warning, because the runner refused the sim and the caller drops the screen. `fork-set-net.test.ts` case 533-S/W covers it. Ticket 535: the optional `ScreenPackage.requestsFor`, which gives every rung its mode sims its own request in one call, so a rung's gems can differ from rung 0's by repair; without it a rung is `request` with its copies, as before. A rung whose request cannot be built writes no warning once the signal has aborted. `fork-meta-repair.test.ts` cases 535-V1 to V5 cover it Ticket 644: header comment only (a dropped set gets no `setBonuses` entry). Ticket 863: the optional `SetScreenInput.onSimFailed(setId, error)`, called for each failed reading except one Stop refused. `fork-set-net.test.ts` cases 511-SF and 511-SA cover it. Ticket 869: a rung request that cannot be built goes to `onRequestNotBuilt` with its error. Review A1 of `fix/867-870-tab-errors` (fork-only): `ScreenPackage.requestsFor` may give undefined for a rung whose gem repair fails, and that rung is not measured, with no line, as when `packageAt` gives no package. E-W3 re-run green. | `seams/sim-runner.ts`  | `seams/sim-runner.ts`                                        | adapted — cache key is canonical-JSON string, no `node:crypto` (D4). Ticket 511 K5R (fork-only, no core ancestor): `SimRunOpts.saveAllValues?` and `SimObservation.allValues?` (each iteration's DPS, asked for only by the set screen), and `simCacheKey` appends `:all` only when `saveAllValues` is true, so no existing key changes. Core's counterpart is untouched; E-W3 compares composed requests, not keys, and re-ran green (`npx vitest run packages/core/test/wowsims-fork-parity.test.ts`). Ticket 535 (fork-only): the optional `SimRunner.computeStats?` and `PlayerStatsObservation`, the first player's final stats, which meta repair reads hit from; `stableStringify` is exported for the set phase's per-request read cache. Parity-safe: E-W3's recorded runner has no `computeStats`; re-run green (`npx vitest run packages/core/test/wowsims-fork-parity.test.ts`) Ticket 567 (fork-only): the bulk screening capability is deleted (owner decision 2026-09-25, ticket 518): the optional bulk method on `SimRunner`, its request and result types, its two error classes, its cache key and `RecordedSimRunner`'s bulk-recordings parameter are gone, so `RecordedSimRunner` takes the same two arguments as core's. Parity-safe: E-W3 constructs `RecordedSimRunner` with two arguments; re-run green before and after (`npx vitest run packages/core/test/wowsims-fork-parity.test.ts`) Ticket 644 (fork-only): optional `SimRunner.activeSetBonuses`; type only. Ticket 830 (fork-only): `SimRunner.computeStats` is required, and `RecordedSimRunner.computeStats` rejects, because recordings hold sims only. E-W3 now passes the fork engine a `RecordedSimRunner` subclass whose read gives 0% hit, so ret's budget is its whole cap and repair values hit at full weight as core does; re-run green (`pnpm exec vitest run packages/core/test/wowsims-fork-parity.test.ts`). Ticket 831 (fork-only): optional `SimObservation.spellDamageBySchool`, its type `SpellDamageBySchool` and `spellDamageBySchool`, which sums a result's first-player action damage by school; E-W3 ranks ret, which does not read it. ## Not ported (plan §2.1)

| `packages/core/src/` file                                          | Why not                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `spec.ts`                                                          | The page _is_ a spec — `PlayerGearSource` (slice 3) reads the page's own current gear under its own selected spec, so there is no talent-classification step to run and nothing to refuse a mismatch against.                                                                 |
| `slots.ts` (`WCL_ORDER`/`mapWclGearToSim` half)                    | The page's `Gear` is already sim-native; no 19→17 WCL translation needed on this surface. (The offline fixtures that inlined it were deleted in ticket 887.)                                                                                                                  |
| `cli.ts`, `seams/cli-sim-runner.ts`                                | CLI entry points; the fork has no CLI.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `seams/store.ts`'s `SqliteStore` half                              | No `node:sqlite` in the browser.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `content-hash.ts`'s `sha256Hex`/`contentHashOf`/`node:crypto` half | D4: cache keys need uniqueness, not a digest; the browser has no `node:crypto`.                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `items.ts`'s 6.8 MB static `data/items/index.json` index           | The fork's own `Database` (`sim.db`) already holds this; see `items.ts`'s adaptation.                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `enchants.ts`'s `data/enchants/index.json` snapshot                | The fork's own `ui/sim/proto/items.ts` (formerly `ui/core/proto_utils/utils.ts`) already exports a live-Database-backed `enchantAppliesToItem`; re-deriving a second copy would itself be the kind of drift plan §3 warns about.                                              |
| `rank-report.ts`, `rank-report-rules.ts`, `rank-report-css.ts`     | CLI/HTML report renderer; the fork's tab is its own renderer (slice 4), not a consumer of packages/core's HTML report. (Ticket 467 removed the last carried-over predicate, `setPotentialIsConfounded`, from `view.ts`; nothing is now imported or inlined from this module.) |

## Data files copied into the fork (plan §2.5)

Not yet done as of this port (slice 2 scope is the `engine/` code surface;
universe/EP-weight data copying is deferred to slice 3, where the adapters
that consume them are built). Recorded here so the gap is visible rather than
silently assumed:

- `data/universes/<spec>-p<N>.json` — **not yet copied**.
- `data/presets/<spec>/p<N>.ep-weights.json` — **not yet copied**.
